question: In a common rail diesel injection system, what is the primary function of the high-pressure accumulator rail?
options: To filter contaminants from the fuel before injection
To maintain a constant high fuel pressure available for all injectors simultaneously
To regulate the quantity of fuel delivered per injection cycle
To cool the fuel before it reaches the injectors

question: When diagnosing an engine with excessive blowby, which combination of tests would most accurately confirm worn piston rings as the root cause?
options: Compression test and cylinder leakage test performed with the piston at BDC
Compression test and cylinder leakage test performed with the piston at TDC on the compression stroke
Vacuum test and oil pressure test performed at idle
Fuel pressure test and injector balance test performed at wide-open throttle

question: A vehicle's ABS warning light illuminates intermittently during braking. A scan tool reveals a fault code for the right-front wheel speed sensor. Which fault is MOST likely causing this condition?
options: Air gap between the sensor and tone ring is too small, causing signal saturation
Excessive reluctor ring runout causing inconsistent signal frequency
Hydraulic modulator solenoid valve stuck in the open position
Master cylinder secondary piston seal failure reducing hydraulic pressure

question: In an automatic transmission, what is the role of a one-way (sprag) clutch during a 1-2 upshift?
options: It locks the turbine shaft to the pump shaft to prevent slippage during high torque
It allows the releasing clutch to overrun smoothly, preventing a harsh shift feel
It mechanically connects the torque converter stator to the transmission case
It prevents reverse gear engagement during forward motion

question: A technician measures 450 mV on the downstream oxygen sensor while the upstream sensor oscillates between 100 mV and 900 mV. What does this indicate?
options: The catalytic converter is functioning correctly and at full efficiency
The downstream sensor has failed and requires replacement
The catalytic converter efficiency has deteriorated below acceptable thresholds
The air-fuel mixture is running excessively lean causing both sensors to read low

question: Which alternator component is responsible for converting the AC voltage generated by the stator windings into DC voltage usable by the vehicle's electrical system?
options: The voltage regulator
The rotor field winding
The rectifier bridge (diode pack)
The slip rings and brush assembly

question: When performing a four-wheel alignment, a vehicle exhibits excessive rear tire wear on the inner edges of both rear tires. Which alignment angle is MOST likely out of specification?
options: Rear toe set excessively toe-out
Rear camber set excessively negative on both sides
Front caster angle set excessively positive
Front scrub radius exceeding manufacturer specification

question: In a variable valve timing (VVT) system using an oil control valve (OCV), what happens when the OCV is commanded fully open by the ECM?
options: Engine oil is directed to the advance chamber of the camshaft phaser, advancing valve timing
Engine oil pressure is reduced to the phaser, causing the camshaft to return to its default position
The camshaft phaser is locked mechanically to prevent timing variation at idle
Engine oil is bypassed entirely to reduce parasitic losses at high RPM

question: A technician is testing a fuel injector using a digital oscilloscope. The waveform shows a normal injector firing spike followed by a prolonged pintle closing time. What does this indicate?
options: The injector solenoid coil has an open circuit
The injector control circuit has excessive resistance causing a slow current build
The injector pintle is sticking open, causing delayed closure and over-fuelling
The fuel pressure is too low, causing the injector to remain partially open

question: During chassis dynamometer testing, a front-wheel-drive vehicle produces significantly less power at the drive wheels than the engine's rated output. Aside from normal drivetrain losses, which component fault would cause the GREATEST additional power loss?
options: A seized brake caliper on one of the driven wheels partially dragging
A faulty crankshaft position sensor causing a 2-degree ignition timing retard
A clogged cabin air filter restricting blower motor airflow
A malfunctioning rear view mirror heating element

question: In a CAN bus network, what is the purpose of the 120-ohm terminating resistors placed at each end of the bus?
options: To step down the 12V supply voltage to the 5V logic level required by ECUs
To prevent signal reflections that would cause data corruption on the network
To limit current draw from the battery during high-speed data transmission
To provide a ground reference for all modules connected to the network

question: A technician notices that a turbocharged engine's boost pressure reaches the correct level but drops off rapidly under sustained wide-open-throttle acceleration. Which fault BEST explains this symptom?
options: A wastegate actuator diaphragm that has ruptured, causing the wastegate to remain closed
An intercooler with internal passages partially blocked, restricting charge air flow
A boost pressure solenoid stuck open, continuously venting boost pressure to atmosphere
A turbocharger compressor wheel with minor tip damage reducing maximum boost

question: When a MacPherson strut front suspension encounters a large bump, which geometric change occurs that helps maintain consistent tyre contact with the road surface?
options: Positive camber increases proportionally to jounce travel to widen the contact patch
Negative camber increases during jounce travel due to the fixed strut upper mount geometry
Caster angle reverses direction to counteract steering pull induced by the bump
Toe angle shifts to maximum toe-in to stabilise the vehicle during rebound

question: A technician performs a relative compression test using a current clamp on the battery positive cable during cranking. What does a cylinder showing a significantly lower current spike compared to other cylinders indicate?
options: That cylinder has higher than normal compression requiring the starter to draw more current
That cylinder has lower compression, requiring less starter motor effort and therefore less current draw
The fuel injector for that cylinder is delivering excess fuel increasing resistance
The spark plug for that cylinder has failed causing a misfire detectable through starter load

question: In a hydraulic power steering system, when the steering wheel is turned and held at full lock, what prevents the power steering pump from being damaged by the resulting pressure build-up?
options: The rack and pinion internal stop limits piston travel before maximum pressure is reached
A pressure relief valve within the pump limits maximum system pressure
The rotary control valve opens fully to bypass fluid directly back to the reservoir
The electric steering motor controller reduces assist torque to zero at full lock
